name: text-3d-flip
title: Text 3D Flip
description: A headline whose letters spring through a 3D flip in a stagger, starting from the first, last, centre or a random glyph, around the axis you choose.
use: A short bold headline should answer the pointer with something more tactile than a colour shift.
avoid: Long or small text, where flipped glyphs hurt reading, and touch screens where hover never fires.
a11y: Visible letters are exposed alongside a full hidden copy, so screen readers repeat the text, and the flip is hover-only. (keyboard: no, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Two left-aligned lines on black: a bold white headline and a smaller grey subheading. Each glyph has its own slot, and while animating some turn edge-on and show a mirrored back face before snapping upright.
behaves: Moving the pointer into the text sets every letter flipping around the chosen axis in a cascade, each springing back to face forward over a few tenths of a second. The sequence runs once per entry and never overlaps itself.
customise: The words are children and the wrapper element is as; rotation axis, stagger origin, stagger spacing, spring transition and class names for both faces are props.
weight: light: One span per character with a spring transform on hover, idle the rest of the time.
demo: The lines "Hover to Flip" and "3D Typography"
issues: Mid-flip letters show a mirrored back face overlapping their neighbours, briefly muddying the line.
polishWhy: The flip has weight and staggers nicely; the mirrored mid-flight glyphs look messy for a beat.
